thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: [PAGER] tenant-checks:aurelia - SLA breach rate exceeded (p95 latency > 1500ms) — 12 instances in last 5m. Pager -> eng-sre oncall

sam_w: I’m on it. seeing a spike of ~40% alerts for Aurelia in the last 10m.

mike_r: grabbing logs. any deploys for their tenant recently?

jia_k: client reported they rolled out a bot that polls more frequently yesterday — might correlate.

nina_p: can someone mute the pager flood while we triage? it's waking multiple folks.

sam_w: temporary silence for the alert group for 10m — doing now. :white_check_mark:

obs-bot: Silence applied: tenant-checks:aurelia for 10 minutes by sam_w. Reason: incident triage.

mike_r: log tail shows repeated 429s from Aurelia API key. backend capacity looks normal, but requests are bursty.

roshan_s: adding that they moved from 30s heartbeat to 5s in prod at 03:10 UTC per support thread.

sam_w: that explains the chattiness. the 'p95 latency > 1500ms' check wasn't scoped to request rate — it's firing because backend queues up. we should avoid paging on rate-driven spikes.

jia_k: propose: create a composite alert that requires p95 latency > 1500ms AND request_rate_per_second > 5 for >3m. otherwise log as warning.

mike_r: agree. quick patch: reduce sensitivity of tenant-checks:aurelia or add rate gating. I'll open a change. snippet:```yaml
alert: tenant-checks-aurelia-sla
expr: max_over_time(p95_latency{tenant="aurelia"}[5m]) > 1.5 and avg_over_time(req_per_s{tenant="aurelia"}[3m]) > 5
for: 3m
severity: page
```

nina_p: also suggest adding a per-tenant debounce for check-heartbeat alerts: if same tenant fires > X times in 5m, escalate only after sustained period.

sam_w: creating dashboard tile in Grafana to show request rate, queue length, p95, and recent deploys for Aurelia. link: https://grafana.internal/d/Aurelia-Tenant (temp)

obs-bot: Dashboard created: Aurelia tenant quick-triage by sam_w.

mike_r: pushed change to staging alert rule. rolling to prod in 2m. will monitor for regressions.

sam_w: FYI I removed the previous immediate page for the existing rule and replaced with a 'warning' channel while we validate the composite rule.

roshan_s: do we need a short-term auto-scaling bump for their dedicated pool? they are in a shared backend with burst quotas.

jia_k: don’t bump yet. first make alert smarter. if after gating we still see true SLA issues we can escalate infra.

mike_r: prod rule update deployed at 1945005678 — composite gating in place. setting 15m watch.

sam_w: monitoring — so far the pager rate dropped to 1/5 previous. latency still blips but not sustained. good sign.

nina_p: can we schedule a follow-up postmortem and a runbook update? add checklist: tenant heartbeat changes, alert gating patterns, dashboard link, product contact.

mike_r: on it. creating a lightweight ticket: INC-1945 "Aurelia: alert gating + runbook update" assigned to eng-sre team. ETA EOD.

obs-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-1945 by mike_r.

sam_w: handoff to next oncall (jia_k) in 25m — I'll debrief them on the gating and dashboard.

jia_k: thanks — will own the 15m watch and follow through with runbook edits. please drop any logs/screenshots in the ticket.

roshan_s: noted for product: I'll ask Aurelia to revert aggressive heartbeat until they adopt back-off.

sam_w: closing silence window. if alerts start firing again, let the pager go through — but we'll rely on composite gating now.

obs-bot: Silence expired: tenant-checks:aurelia (was applied by sam_w).

mike_r: quick postmortem notes (for ticket): root cause = tenant-side change increasing poll rate; impact = transient paging noise and potential SLA blips; mitigation = composite alert to gate on rate + latency, dashboard for triage, runbook update, product outreach.

nina_p: adding one more action: add test harness in staging that simulates high-frequency heartbeats per-tenant so we can tune thresholds without noisy prod pages.

sam_w: good call. I’ll add that to INC-1945 and schedule 1h sync tomorrow with product and SRE.

jia_k: all set from my side. leaving notes in the ticket and marking the thread resolved. :thumbsup:

sam_w: resolved — closing thread.
